answer: In a market for falcon sightings near a marble quarry, trust grows through a thread of completed, paid jobs with distinct buyers. Each buyer has a fixed endorsement budget per epoch, and payouts depend on verified work and those scarce endorsements, not seller names. Splitting one seller into ten aliases divides the same buyers' budgets; gaining more weight requires recruiting real paying customers, paying fees, and delivering separate evidence. A cartel could self-deal to simulate demand, so reciprocal trades are discounted and random sightings are independently checked.
